models.description: QPSK resource-block groups (x = 40 % of the PRBs) are boosted by 3 dB, the remaining PRBs are de-boosted so that the total power equals that of N_RB-3 PRBs at 0 dB; n_RNTI 2 occupies PRB 0-2.

fixed_parameters.value: n_RNTI 0: boosted QPSK RBGs (type 0 allocation) (QPSK); n_RNTI 1: de-boosted QPSK PRBs (type 0 allocation) (QPSK); n_RNTI 2: PRB 0-2, symbols from 2 (PRBs below the full-band user) (QPSK)

fixed_parameters.name: Target share x
fixed_parameters.value: 40 % of the PRBs 3...N_RB-1 (resource-block groups of n_RNTI 0)

fixed_parameters.name: RBG size P
fixed_parameters.value: TS 38.214 table 5.1.2.2.1-1 configuration 1 with N_RB-3 PRBs: 2 (up to 36), 4 (up to 72), 8 (up to 144), 16 (up to 275)

fixed_parameters.name: Number of target RBGs
fixed_parameters.value: N_RBG = min(floor(x (N_RB-3) / P), (A - A mod 2) / 2 + 1), A = floor((N_RB-3 + (3 mod P) - P) / P)

fixed_parameters.name: Target RBG locations
fixed_parameters.value: RBG floor((N_RB-3 + (3 mod P)) / P) - 1 and, if N_RBG > 1, RBG 1, 3, ..., 2 (N_RBG-2) + 1 (0-based, RBG 0 being the partial first group that starts at PRB 3)

fixed_parameters.name: Level of the target RBGs
fixed_parameters.value: +3 dB (n_RNTI 0)

fixed_parameters.name: Level of the other PRBs
fixed_parameters.value: n_RNTI 1: 10 log10((N_RB-3 - 10^(3/10) P N_RBG) / (N_RB-3 - P N_RBG)) dB so that the total power equals N_RB-3 PRBs at 0 dB

models.description: NR-FR1-TM1.1 on the NR carrier with one NR resource block punctured by an NB-IoT carrier (TS 36.141 N-TM) at the eligible position closest to the minimum guard band; the NB-IoT resource elements are boosted by X dB over the average resource element. Studio generates FDD with 15 kHz only; the standard also defines a TDD form that is not implemented.

fixed_parameters.name: Users (table 4.9.2.3.2-1)
fixed_parameters.value: n_RNTI 0: PRB 3 to N_RB-1 (all PRBs outside the control-channel PRBs), symbols from 0 (QPSK); n_RNTI 2: PRB 0-2, symbols from 2 (PRBs below the full-band user) (QPSK)

fixed_parameters.name: Level
fixed_parameters.value: 0 dB boost on all PRBs

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT
fixed_parameters.value: one NR resource block per NB-IoT carrier is punctured at the eligible in-band position closest to the lower and/or upper minimum guard band (L_NB-IoT, R_NB-IoT) and carries the NB-IoT test model N-TM of TS 36.141 6.1.3-6.1.6, the only NB-IoT test model there is; every other NR carrier is NR-FR1-TM1.1

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT channels
fixed_parameters.value: NPSS, NSSS, NRS, NPBCH, NPDCCH (format 1) and NPDSCH (single user, n_RNTI 1000, QPSK), normal cyclic prefix, n_f = 0 and slot 0 at the start; all data bits are zero (scrambled as in TS 36.211 clause 10.2)

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT subframe map
fixed_parameters.value: one 10 ms frame repeated every frame: subframe 0 NPBCH, 1 NPDCCH, 2-4 and 6-8 NPDSCH, 5 NPSS, 9 NSSS; NRS in every subframe except 5 and 9

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT antenna port
fixed_parameters.value: one NB-IoT antenna port is exported (NRS port 2000); the 304 (stand-alone) / 200 (in-band) bit budgets of TS 36.141 6.1.4 are those of a two-port NRS, four host CRS ports and three control symbols, so the NRS positions of port 2001 stay reserved and only the 100 data resource elements per in-band subframe are used

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT cell identity
fixed_parameters.value: N_ID^Ncell = 97 + 6 n + max(0, m - 1) with m the cell identity of the host NR carrier and n the rank of the host among the NB-IoT hosts (103 for the lowest host with cell identity 1, 110 for the second); the lower and the upper NB-IoT carrier of one host share it; at most 503

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT resource elements
fixed_parameters.value: 1085 of the 1680 N_RB resource elements of a frame per NB-IoT carrier: 108 (100 data + 8 NRS) in each of the eight subframes 0-4 and 6-8, NPSS 105 and NSSS 116; 1089 if the host cell identity mod 6 is 2 or 5 (the NPSS then skips no host CRS resource element)

fixed_parameters.name: NB-IoT power
fixed_parameters.value: P_avg = P_rated / (12 N_RB); NB-IoT RE: P_avg 10^(X/10); NR RE: (P_rated - N_NB-IoT P_NB-IoT) / N_NR, counted over the resource elements of the whole 10 ms frame. X is the manufacturer's declared NB-IoT power dynamic range, at least 6 dB at the positions L_NB-IoT and R_NB-IoT of host carriers up to 20 MHz and at least 3 dB for 25 MHz and wider (TS 38.104 Table 6.3.4.2-1, TS 38.141-1 D.43). Studio enforces that minimum and accepts X up to 12 dB: the upper limit is a Studio limit, the standard sets none

fixed_parameters.name: NR content around NB-IoT
fixed_parameters.value: NR-FR1-TM1.1 on every resource element without NB-IoT signal, including the control symbols and host CRS positions of the punctured resource block

fixed_parameters.name: Duplex / numerology
fixed_parameters.value: Studio generates FDD with 15 kHz subcarrier spacing and channel bandwidths of 3 to 50 MHz. The standard also defines a TDD form (TS 38.141-1 Table 4.9.2.2-1a: D S U U D at 15 kHz, 5 ms); Studio does not implement NB-IoT in-band operation with TDD in this release. The NB-IoT bandwidth of 180 kHz is one NR resource block only at 15 kHz, which is why other numerologies are not offered

used_for: Unwanted emissions > Operating band unwanted emissions

users.role: PRB 3 to N_RB-1 (all PRBs outside the control-channel PRBs), symbols from 0
PRB 0-2, symbols from 2 (PRBs below the full-band user)

notes: Models of 3GPP TS 38.141-1 V18.14.0 clause 4.9.2.2 (FR1, BS type 1-C and 1-H); N_RB from TS 38.104 table 5.3.2-1. The FR2 models of TS 38.141-2 are not included.

Parameters you can set: duplex mode, number of carriers, subcarrier spacing and channel bandwidth per carrier, the gap before a carrier (sub-block gap), rank for NR-FR1-TM1.1, the PN23 conventions, NB-IoT position and boost, oversampling and capture length. Studio extensions, not options of the standard: a cell identity other than N_ID^cell = n for the n-th lowest carrier (TS 38.141-1 4.9.2.3; flagged in the warnings), at most 16 carriers and an NB-IoT boost of at most 12 dB (the standard sets neither limit).

Carriers are placed at the nominal channel spacing of TS 38.104 5.4.1.2 for 100 kHz-raster bands, the aggregate is centred at baseband DC and every carrier has the same resource-element amplitude (equal power spectral density).
Only PDCCH, PDSCH and DM-RS are generated: no SSB, CSI-RS, PT-RS or channel coding; the NRTC6 ON-OFF patterns are not included.
At most 1,000,000 samples are generated: the capture is shortened to whole subframes, or lower the oversampling.

Not offered: NR-N-TM with TDD (defined in TS 38.141-1 Table 4.9.2.2-1a), the channel spacing rules of 15 kHz and 60 kHz raster bands (TS 38.104 5.4.1.2; Studio uses the 100 kHz-raster rule), a PN23 stream shared by all users, and the NRTC1-6 configurations as such.
